name: sol_basics_al_8
description: Off-by-one boundary errors in the first or last loop iteration
question: The source file in `source` contains a loop over an array or collection whose first or last iteration is handled with an incorrect or inconsistent boundary condition (e.g., wrong start index, wrong end bound, or a special-cased first/last element treated differently from the rest), causing an element to be skipped, double-processed, or accessed out of bounds, with a resulting incorrect calculation, missed state update, or out-of-bounds read/write, excluding loops whose bounds are correct and behave consistently across all iterations.
criteria: a for-loop starts at index 1 instead of 0, causing the first array element to be skipped in a balance, reward, or sum computation
a loop's condition uses `i <= array.length` instead of `i < array.length`, causing an out-of-bounds access on the last iteration
a loop computes its end bound as length-1 when it should be length (or vice versa), causing the last element to be skipped or double-counted
the last iteration of a loop is handled by separate special-case code that applies different logic than the rest of the loop, producing an inconsistent result for that element
a loop that removes or shifts array elements updates the length or index incorrectly on the final iteration, skipping the last element during processing
